title: Factor-geometry scaling of deterministic structural routing
question: Can increasing product-key factorization depth reduce exact-address routing work while preserving the held-out execution capability recovered in frontier 002?
hypothesis: The dense exact-address region in the three-factor index is caused by factor-cell collisions. More factor partitions with controlled beam width should reduce exact-address candidates and total route arithmetic, with PST retained as the transition-compatibility scorer.

task_protocol.evaluation: 80 unique-target held-out toggle tasks per seed/M cell
task_protocol.transition_scorer: PST trained only on verified training transitions

held_constant: PST model and training records unchanged from frontier 002
unique-target task construction unchanged from frontier 002
no SECA or verifier feedback in single-step routing

decision_rule.condition: Report execution_success and all routing arithmetic for every geometry at every M and absolute budget.
decision_rule.does_not_license: C5 or asymptotic claims unless total routing work and internal address work both stop increasing with M.

decision_rule.condition: A geometry is a candidate for the next phase only if its capability curve is competitive with the frontier-002 structural+PST control and its internal address fraction is materially lower at larger M.
decision_rule.licenses: selection of an engineering configuration for further testing.
